header.name: Tata Consumer Products Ltd
header.source: NSE closing price (end of day, not live); 52-week range computed from daily highs and lows (NSE bhavcopy)

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Tata Consumer Products (NSE: TATACONSUM), part of the Tata Group, sells branded tea, coffee, water and food products in India and abroad; its consolidated revenue in FY26 was ₹20,290 crore.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: In the quarter to 30 Sep 2026, revenue was ₹5,661 crore, 14.0% more than a year earlier; the operating margin was 10.9% against 10.4%, and profit attributable to shareholders was ₹469 crore, 16.0% higher.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: On 27 Oct 2026, the first session after the result, TATACONSUM shares rose 6.78% while the NIFTY 50 fell 0.02% and the NIFTY FMCG index rose 0.74%; allowing for the market's move, TATACONSUM's own move was +6.83%, about 4.95 times its usual daily variation.

claims.label: UNCERTAIN
claims.text: These numbers measure the move, not its cause: the result, the FMCG sector's rise and any other news that day overlap, and nothing here separates them.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: Neither discounted cash flow template used on this site applies to TATACONSUM: Template A needs free cash flow to the firm to be positive in at least three of the last four years, and it was −₹1,628 crore in FY24 and −₹949 crore in FY25; Template B, for companies reinvesting at a return above their cost of capital, needs the median return on invested capital of the last three years to beat that cost, and it was 8.3% against 9.89%, so no model value is shown.

claims.label: FACT
claims.text: Those two years include the acquisitions of Capital Foods (three-quarters of it in Q4 FY24, the rest to be bought within three years) and Organic India (completed in Q1 FY25); the template counts money spent on acquisitions as reinvestment, like capital spending.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: At ₹1,085 (NSE close, 12 Nov 2026), the shares traded at 63.2× the profit attributable to shareholders over the last four reported quarters.

claims.label: CALCULATION
claims.text: Free cash flow to the firm was ₹483 crore in FY26; Template A would apply once it has been positive in three of the last four years, and the Q3 FY27 result will be the next reported quarter.

prices.note: Each series is rebased to 100 on the first common session. Raw exchange prices are not published here (NSE terms).

metrics.label: Market cap
metrics.definition: Price × shares outstanding (share capital ÷ ₹1 face value at 2026-09-30).

metrics.label: P/E (TTM)
metrics.definition: Price ÷ earnings per share over the last four reported quarters (Q3 FY26 – Q2 FY27).

metrics.label: EV / EBIT (TTM)
metrics.definition: Enterprise value (market cap − the net cash and treasury figure below) ÷ operating profit over the last four quarters.

metrics.label: Net cash and treasury
metrics.definition: Cash, bank balances and treasury investments, plus investments in joint ventures and associates, less lease liabilities, borrowings, preference shares and minority interests, at 30 Sep 2026.

metrics.label: Operating margin (FY26)
metrics.definition: EBIT ÷ revenue, after depreciation, excluding other income. Sites that quote an EBITDA-based margin show a higher figure.

metrics.label: ROE (FY26)
metrics.definition: Profit for the year ÷ total equity at year end.

metrics.label: ROIC (FY26)
metrics.definition: After-tax EBIT ÷ invested capital at the start of the year. Invested capital excludes about ₹3k crore of cash and treasury.

metrics.label: Revenue growth FY22–FY26
metrics.definition: Compound annual growth of revenue from FY22 to FY26.

metrics.label: Cash conversion (FY26)
metrics.definition: Operating cash flow ÷ profit for the year.

metrics.label: Beta vs NIFTY 50
metrics.definition: Sensitivity of TATACONSUM's daily return to the NIFTY 50's, over the two years to the price date.

reasons: free cash flow not positive in at least 3 of the last 4 years
valuation.b_template: B (reinvestment phase, return on capital above its cost)
b_reasons: median return on invested capital over the last 3 years (8.3%) is not above the cost of capital (9.89%), so growth would not add value
valuation.note: Neither Template A nor Template B applies, so no DCF value, scenario, reverse DCF or sensitivity is computed.

limitations: Two templates (A: positive free cash flow; B: reinvestment earning above its cost), and neither applies here. Banks, insurers and holding companies have no template yet.
Debt is borrowings plus lease liabilities; earmarked bank balances are counted as cash, which overstates cash slightly.
The event study measures the size of a move, not its cause; five results days are too few for statistical claims.
Other financial liabilities include the obligation to acquire the remaining quarter of Capital Foods; it is not counted as debt here.
Non-current investments are mostly equity holdings; they are treated as non-operating, like cash, and so leave invested capital.
From FY23 the figures come from the exchange XBRL filings; the FY22 balance sheet and the FY23–FY25 lease lines come from the results PDFs.
